item.title: OpenRouter Removes Three AI Providers After Data‑Handling Violations
item.description:
OpenRouter Removes Three AI Providers After Data‑Handling Violations

OpenRouter removed three AI providers from its platform after discovering they had violated data‑handling policies and exposed sensitive data.

🔍 Overview

  • OpenRouter revoked Zero Data Retention (ZDR) eligibility for 125 endpoints as a precaution.
  • The company notified all potentially affected customers.
  • OpenRouter removed the leaking inference providers: Together AI, Phala, and Novita.
  • Atlas Cloud voluntarily withdrew its models from OpenRouter pending security testing.

🧩 How it Works

  • OpenRouter is an AI model broker that lets developers access models from different companies using a single API key.
  • When an app sends a request, OpenRouter forwards it to the provider that runs the selected model and passes the answer back.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Dragos alerted OpenRouter after sending two million test prompts containing unique tracking links or decoy credentials.
  • Dragos detected activity indicating data from at least three AI providers was exposed.
  • Dragos found that in some cases credentials were leaked to outsiders and used in the wild.
  • Dragos said: “We observed activity indicating that data from at least three AI providers was exposed. Our seeded test prompts were used in attempts to access our controlled test systems and canary AWS accounts.”
  • OpenRouter said there was no breach on its own systems, pointing the leak to the provider level.
  • The providers’ incidents and responses:
Provider Incident Response
Together AI Exposed a GitHub repository credential, allowing unauthorized download of prompt samples (June–July) involving MiniMax M3, GLM‑5.2, Kimi K2.6 Tightening security controls; strengthening zero‑data retention; advising users to rotate secrets
Phala Server processing DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 requests compromised; credentials obtained from affected VMs (Oct 21‑22, possibly up to Nov 8) Tightening security controls; strengthening zero‑data retention; advising users to rotate secrets
Novita Routing misconfiguration forwarded MiniMax requests to MiniMax’s official API (May 28‑Nov 11) Tightening security controls; strengthening zero‑data retention; advising users to rotate secrets
Atlas Cloud Voluntarily withdrew models pending security testing after a third‑party incident —
  • All four providers are tightening security controls, strengthening their zero‑data retention or data deletion policies, and advising potentially impacted users to rotate any secrets that may have been exposed.
  • OpenRouter is adapting Dragos’ tests for ongoing use to check whether AI providers forward or leak user requests/responses to third parties.
  • OpenRouter will require validation before restoring ZDR eligibility.

💡 Why it Matters

  • The leaks exposed sensitive data and credentials to unauthorized parties, highlighting the importance of strict data‑handling policies for AI model brokers.
  • OpenRouter’s response—removing the offending providers, revoking ZDR eligibility, and adopting continuous testing—illustrates how platform operators can mitigate risks when provider security is compromised.

#OpenRouter #AI #DataSecurity #ModelBroker #ZeroDataRetention

Source: OpenRouter drops AI providers over leaked prompts and secrets

item.title: New Dockerized React/FastAPI app replicates LLM Council for model comparison
item.description:
New Dockerized React/FastAPI app replicates LLM Council for model comparison

A new React/FastAPI application is available for comparing model answers, peer rankings, and a chairman’s synthesis, inspired by Andrej Karpathy’s LLM Council concept.

🧩 How it works

The application allows each conversation to select OpenRouter or Ollama, its specific models, system prompts, and an execution mode. It supports persistent conversations, attachments, and streaming with cancellation and partial-result recovery. Execution is handled through bounded and idempotent model runs, with runtime settings controlled by administrators.

⚙️ Key details

  • Dependencies: The project uses a committed uv.lock and frontend/package-lock.json to ensure reproducible dependencies.
  • TOON statistics: Token representation comparisons are provided, but these are explicitly not provider billing.
  • Ports: The backend is published loopback-only at http://127.0.0.1:8001, while the frontend is published on port 80.
  • Proxy Limits: The frontend nginx.conf and optional nginx/nginx.conf files both set client_max_body_size to 25m. A 20 MiB image becomes approximately 26.7 MiB in base64, which can successfully upload but receive a 413 error at the proxy. To support the full API image limit, the setting must be increased to 40m and the proxy layer rebuilt.
  • Resources: The backend container has a 1 GiB total memory limit in Compose. PDF workers on Linux can each have a 1 GiB virtual-memory ceiling, with two workers per API process.
  • Databases: Compose does not provision PostgreSQL or MySQL servers. Adding PostgreSQL requires exporting base runtime dependencies with --extra database and rebuilding the image. Finance and embeddings extras similarly require explicit image packaging.
  • Environments: Python 3.10+ is declared by the project, with CI and the backend image using 3.12. Node 20.19+ or 22.12+ is required by the locked Vite release; the frontend image uses Node 22, while CI tests Node 20.
  • Configuration: In Docker, keeping a specific build-time setting empty utilizes the same-origin nginx proxy. Changing this setting for built assets requires a rebuild.

🚀 Availability

Running the application requires a running Docker engine and current Docker Compose v2. The default backend Dockerfile exports base runtime dependencies only.

#OpenRouter #Ollama #Docker #FastAPI #LLMCouncil

Source: DmitryBMsk/llm-council-plus

item.title: OpenRouter Model Routing and Provider Control Features
item.description:
OpenRouter Model Routing and Provider Control Features

OpenRouter provides an API endpoint that automatically handles fallbacks and selects the most cost-effective option for model requests.

⚙️ Key details

Because different providers use various serving software, optimizations, and settings, the same OpenRouter endpoint can result in requests that behave in different ways. These differences include:

  • Some providers lack vision capability for vision models.
  • The processing of the reasoning effort option can differ between providers.

🧩 How it works

Users have tools to manage how their requests are routed:

  • provider.only option: Allows users to control which specific provider is routed to.
  • /endpoints method: Returns a list of available providers for a specific model ID.

#OpenRouter #API #LLM #ModelRouting

Source: So you want to use OpenRouter?
